name: table
title: Table
description: Semantic, controlled data table with durable visual primitives for density, column geometry, grouping, sorting, multi-selection, sticky overflow, and incremental loading.

intent.summary: Semantic, controlled data table with durable visual primitives for density, column geometry, grouping, sorting, multi-selection, sticky overflow, and incremental loading.
useWhen: A structured dataset needs native row and column relationships, optional one-level grouping, or comparable values across records.
An application needs controlled sorting, loaded-row selection, or lazy loading while retaining ownership of the data query and transformations.
A product table needs a token-backed recipe whose individual header, group, row, cell, selection, state, and load-more layers remain easy to restyle.
avoidWhen: Content is primarily editorial prose; use semantic product-owned markup with the prose recipe instead.
A small label/value set reads more clearly as a list, description list, or card.
The interface requires tree-grid behavior, nested grouping, inline cell editing, row reordering, column pinning, or virtualization; those are outside this first contract.
The application expects the component to fetch, paginate, sort, group, or mutate records internally.
accessibility: The rendered structure uses a native table, caption, column headers, row groups, and data cells; keep the caption non-empty even when it is visually hidden.
Sorting controls remain buttons inside column headers. Member-row sort uses aria-sort, while independent group order is described by the grouped header control.
Selection controls expose checkbox semantics and explicit row names; select-all affects selectable loaded rows only and preserves selected identities outside the loaded window.
Scrollable table regions become keyboard focusable and named only when overflow exists.
Incremental loading, newly appended row counts, failures, and end-of-results transitions are announced through a polite status region without replacing visible state.
states: Columns, rows, groups, grouping, sorting, selected row IDs, and lazy-loading state are controlled inputs. Events communicate intent and never mutate those inputs.
Grouping supports one level. The application supplies ordered groups and ordered member rows; group order and member-row sort are independent controls.
Sort activation cycles ascending, descending, and clear for ordinary columns. The grouped column toggles ascending and descending group order without clearing member sort.

Initial loading uses row-shaped skeletons. Empty and initial error states remain inside the table. Incremental loading retains existing rows and supports automatic sentinel, manual load-more, retry, and terminal states.
Lazy loading replaces pagination. The application owns requests, cancellation, cursors, deduplication, appended records, and query identity; loadIdentity resets the component request guard.
Cells accept scalar content or a standard primary-and-secondary text primitive. Nullish values render a visible em dash with localized assistive text.
The public @ds-mo/ui/table.css export is the authoritative zero-specificity visual recipe. Override its --ds-table-* properties or target its stable element classes for product-specific styling.
responsiveBehavior: The table keeps native semantics at narrow widths and scrolls horizontally instead of transforming into cards.
Explicit column sizes establish the horizontal overflow width; unsized columns share remaining space.
Medium and small density adjust header, row, padding, and selection geometry without changing behavior or content hierarchy.
Long content truncates by default and can opt into wrapping at the column or cell level.

customElements: Assign columns, rows, groups, grouping, sort, and selectedRowIds through JavaScript properties rather than HTML attribute strings.
Replace controlled property values in response to dsSortChange, dsGroupingChange, dsSelectionChange, and dsLoadMore.
react: Pass new array and state-object references when the controlled data or query state changes.
Apply the emitted detail to application state and perform sorting, grouping, or loading in the data layer.
angular: Bind complex table inputs as properties and update the controlled values from the corresponding output events.
Keep server cursor and query lifecycle state in the owning service or container.

caption.description: Required accessible table name, rendered as a native caption.

columns.description: Stable column definitions. Assign through JavaScript.

error.description: Initial error state. Existing rows stay visible; incremental failures use loadMoreError.

grouping.description: Controlled grouping column and group-order direction.

groups.description: One level of application-owned grouped data. Assign through JavaScript.

lazyLoading.description: Enable application-owned incremental loading without pagination.

loadIdentity.description: Reset key for a new query/group/sort dataset.

loadMoreThreshold.description: IntersectionObserver root margin in CSS pixels.

loading.description: Initial loading state. Existing rows stay visible; incremental loading uses loadingMore.

maxHeight.description: Maximum scroll-region height. Numbers resolve to CSS pixels.

rows.description: Ungrouped row data. Ignored while grouping is active. Assign through JavaScript.

scrollLabel.description: Optional explicit label for the horizontal/vertical scroll region.

selectedRowIds.description: Controlled selected row identities. IDs outside the loaded rows are preserved.
